# Part 1: Template, VFD Pump Control Narrative

**Convention:** Values in `{braces}` are looked up in the I/O list or alarm database, not typed here. Engineers write only the *behavior*: what causes what, and why. If a setpoint changes in the spreadsheet, the narrative should not need editing.

---

**1. Identification**
| Item | Entry |
|---|---|
| Module tag | |
| Service / description | |
| Source → Destination | |
| Drive tag / Motor tag | |
| Revision / date / author | |

**2. Purpose**
One or two sentences: what the pump does in the process and who commands it.

**3. Associated instruments and devices**
| Tag | Function in this module | Used for (permissive / trip / control / indication only) |
|---|---|---|
| | | |

Include the VFD's hardwired and networked signals (run command, ready, running, fault, speed ref, speed feedback, local/remote).

**4. Modes**
- **Auto:** who commands it (batch / sequence / other), what commands are accepted.
- **Manual:** operator start/stop and speed from HMI. State which interlocks remain active.
- **Out of service / Maintenance:** what it does to commands and alarms.
- **Local (field selector/VFD keypad):** what the PLC sees and does.

**5. States**
List states (e.g., Stopped, Starting, Running, Stopping, Faulted) and the transition conditions for each.

**6. Start permissives** (all must be true; pump will not start otherwise)
| # | Condition | Tag(s) | Reason | Shown to operator as |
|---|---|---|---|---|

**7. Run interlocks / trips** (pump stops or is inhibited when true)
| # | Condition | Tag(s) | Delay | Action | Reset type (auto / manual) | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

**8. Speed control**
- Speed reference source per mode.
- Limits, ramp rates, minimum run speed (`{from I/O list}`).
- Behavior on loss of reference or bad-quality signal.

**9. Start and stop sequence**
Numbered steps, including start-fail timeout, stop-fail timeout, and minimum off-time or restart limits.

**10. Alarms**
Reference the alarm database by tag. Narrative lists only the *behavior* not captured there.
| Alarm (DB ID/tag) | Causes the module to… | Operator expectation |
|---|---|---|

**11. Instrument failure handling**
For each instrument: behavior on bad quality, out-of-range, or wire break, and whether bypass is permitted.

**12. Power loss / restart / comms loss**
State after power-up, after PLC restart, and after loss of batch-system communication.

**13. Interfaces to other modules**
Signals exchanged with the batch system or neighboring modules (commands, status, faults) and their meaning.

**14. HMI**
Operator actions available, faceplate indications, and any bypass or override with required privilege level.

**15. Test points (for FAT/SAT)**
One line per permissive, trip, and failure case, each checkable.

**16. Open items / deviations from standard**

---

# Part 2: Filled Example, P-1102

**1. Identification**
| Item | Entry |
|---|---|
| Module tag | P-1102 |
| Service | Transfer pump |
| Source → Destination | Mix tank T-110 → Hold tank T-120 |
| Drive / Motor | per I/O list (VFD, speed reference from batch system) |
| Revision | Draft A |

**2. Purpose**
P-1102 transfers product from T-110 to T-120 at a speed set by the batch system. It is protected against running dry, deadheading, and overfilling the destination tank.

**3. Associated instruments and devices**
| Tag | Function | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| LSL-110 | T-110 low level switch | Permissive and trip (dry-run protection) |
| PT-1102 | Pump discharge pressure | Trip (high), trip/alarm (low while running); indication |
| LSH-120 | T-120 high level switch | Permissive and trip (overfill protection) |
| P-1102 VFD signals | Run cmd, ready, running, fault, speed ref, speed fb, local/remote | Control and status |

**4. Modes**
- **Auto:** Batch system issues run/stop and speed reference. All permissives and trips active.
- **Manual:** Operator starts/stops and sets speed from HMI. All permissives and trips remain active.
- **Out of service:** Pump cannot be started. Its alarms are suppressed except VFD fault. Entry and exit are logged. Batch system sees the module as unavailable.
- **Local:** If the VFD or field selector is in local, the PLC reports "Local", ignores run/speed commands, and still monitors the trips. Whether the PLC can stop a locally run pump depends on the drive wiring (see Open Items).

**5. States**
- **Stopped:** no run command output.
- **Starting:** run command issued, waiting for drive running feedback.
- **Running:** drive running feedback confirmed.
- **Stopping:** run command removed, waiting for drive stopped feedback.
- **Faulted:** a trip or drive fault is active and has not been reset.

**6. Start permissives**
| # | Condition | Tag | Reason | Operator message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | T-110 level not low (LSL-110 satisfied) | LSL-110 | Prevent dry run | "T-110 level low" |
| 2 | T-120 not high (LSH-120 not active) | LSH-120 | Prevent overfill | "T-120 level high" |
| 3 | VFD ready, no drive fault | VFD signals | Drive able to run | "Drive not ready" |
| 4 | Module not out of service and in Auto or Manual (not Local) | Mode | Control authority | "Not in remote" |
| 5 | No latched trip awaiting reset | Module | Force operator review | "Trip active, reset required" |

**7. Run interlocks / trips**
| # | Condition | Tag | Delay | Action | Reset | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | T-110 low level | LSL-110 | `{delay}` to avoid slosh nuisance trips | Stop pump | Auto-clears when level returns; pump does **not** auto-restart. New start command required | Dry-run protection |
| 2 | T-120 high level | LSH-120 | `{delay}` | Stop pump | Same as above | Overfill protection |
| 3 | Discharge pressure high | PT-1102 | `{delay}` | Stop pump | Manual | Blocked discharge or deadhead |
| 4 | Discharge pressure low while running above minimum speed | PT-1102 | `{delay, longer than start-up ramp}` | Stop pump | Manual | Loss of prime, dry running not caught by LSL-110, or line break |
| 5 | Drive fault | VFD | None | Stop pump | Manual, after drive fault is cleared | Equipment protection |
| 6 | Start fail: no running feedback in `{timeout}` | VFD | `{timeout}` | Remove run cmd, fault | Manual | Drive not responding |
| 7 | Unexpected stop: running feedback lost without a stop command | VFD | Short debounce | Fault | Manual | Drive or motor problem |

PT-1102 low-pressure monitoring is inhibited during the start-up ramp and re-enabled after the `{delay}` once running.

**8. Speed control**
- **Auto:** speed reference comes from the batch system.
- **Manual:** speed set by the operator on the HMI.
- Reference is clamped to the min/max in the I/O list. Ramp times are set in the drive, as listed in the I/O list.
- If the batch reference is bad quality or the comms heartbeat is lost, the pump holds its last speed for `{time}`, then stops with an alarm (see section 12). Confirm this with the process owner.

**9. Start and stop sequence**
1. Start command received (batch or operator).
2. Check permissives 1–5. If any fail, reject the command and display the first failing message.
3. Write the speed reference (clamped), then issue the run command.
4. Wait for running feedback within `{timeout}`. If it is not received, trip 6.
5. After the start-up delay, enable the PT-1102 low-pressure trip.
6. Stop command or any trip removes the run command. The drive decelerates per its configured stop mode.
7. Stop confirmed by drive feedback within `{timeout}`, otherwise raise a stop-fail alarm.

A restart after any stop requires a fresh command. Any minimum off-time or starts-per-hour limit comes from `{I/O list}`.

**10. Alarms** (setpoints, priorities, and text are in the alarm database)
| Alarm | Module behavior | Operator expectation |
|---|---|---|
| T-110 low level | Trip 1 | Check tank supply, restart when level recovered |
| T-120 high level | Trip 2 | Check downstream transfer; restart when level clears |
| Discharge pressure high | Trip 3 | Check discharge line and valves; reset |
| Discharge pressure low | Trip 4 | Check prime and line integrity; reset |
| Drive fault | Trip 5 | Check drive; clear fault; reset |
| Start fail / stop fail / unexpected stop | Trips 6 and 7 | Inspect pump and drive |
| PT-1102 bad quality | See section 11 | Check instrument |

**11. Instrument failure handling**
- **LSL-110 / LSH-120:** Switch logic must be fail-safe (wire break reads as the unsafe condition: low level or high level). Wire break or discrepancy therefore stops the pump and blocks starting. No bypass.
- **PT-1102:** On bad quality or out-of-range, raise the instrument alarm, disable the low-pressure trip, and **keep** the high-pressure trip function only if a valid reading exists. Otherwise block starting in Auto. Maintenance bypass is allowed for the low-pressure trip only, at supervisor privilege level, with a time limit and logging. *(Proposed; confirm with the process owner.)*

**12. Power loss / restart / comms loss**
- After power-up or PLC restart: pump is Stopped with no run command. No auto restart.
- Loss of batch comms in Auto: see section 8. Pump does not continue running indefinitely on stale data.
- Drive power loss: treated as unexpected stop (trip 7).

**13. Interfaces**
| Signal | Direction | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Run request / stop request | Batch → module | Command |
| Speed reference | Batch → module | Setpoint |
| Heartbeat | Both | Comms health |
| Running / Faulted / Available / Permissive-OK | Module → batch | Status. Batch should not wait on a pump that reports Faulted or unavailable |
| Interlock reason code | Module → batch | Lets the batch report why a start was rejected |

**14. HMI**
- Faceplate shows mode, state, speed reference and feedback, PT-1102 value, and the status of each permissive and trip.
- Operator actions: Start, Stop, Reset, speed entry (Manual), mode selection.
- Out of service and PT-1102 low-pressure bypass require supervisor privilege and are logged.
- Permissives and trips cannot be overridden from the HMI.

**15. Test points**
1. Start with LSL-110 low: rejected, correct message.
2. Start with LSH-120 high: rejected.
3. Start with drive not ready: rejected.
4. Running, drive LSL-110 low past delay: pump stops, no auto restart when level returns.
5. Running, LSH-120 high: pump stops.
6. Running, PT-1102 simulated high: pump stops, manual reset needed.
7. Running, PT-1102 simulated low after start-up delay: pump stops.
8. PT-1102 low simulated *during* start-up ramp: no trip.
9. Disconnect LSL-110 and LSH-120 wires: pump stops or is blocked.
10. Drive fault: pump faults, reset needs drive fault clear.
11. Prevent running feedback: start-fail trip at timeout.
12. Break batch heartbeat in Auto: behavior matches section 8.
13. Power-cycle PLC while running: pump stopped on restart.
14. Local mode: PLC reports Local and ignores commands.
15. Speed reference outside limits: clamped.

**16. Open items**
- Are there suction or discharge valves in this line-up? None were given, so no valve-position permissives are included. If any exist (for example a T-120 inlet valve), add them as permissives and to the discharge-pressure-high logic.
- Confirm the delay values and the bad-quality hold time in section 8.
- Confirm whether the PLC can stop the drive when it is in local (hardwired enable vs. network only).
- Confirm that LSL-110 and LSH-120 are wired fail-safe.
- Confirm whether the pressure-low trip should fault or only alarm below a certain speed, since low speed gives low pressure.

---

**Notes on using the template**
- I did not invent setpoints, tags, or delays. Every `{…}` should map to a column in your I/O list or alarm database. Consider adding a check that fails if the narrative contains a literal number that should come from a spreadsheet.
- Sections 4, 5, 9, 12, 13, and 14 will be identical or nearly so for most pumps. You could move them into a project-level standard and have the per-pump document only reference it, leaving engineers to fill in sections 1–3, 6–8, 10–11, and 15–16.
